title: Consolidated Enterprise Request Intake & Rapid-Scoping Playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook and tooling pattern for Sales/Customer Success to aggregate enterprise non-bug feature requests, perform initial prioritization, and hand off scoped epics to Product/Engineering. Goal is to reduce friction, align requests to measurable business outcomes, and shorten time-to-scope for high-value customers.

Background: We see frequent enterprise asks coming through Sales and CS (RBAC, private deploy workflow tweaks, audit log formats, SLA contract changes). Currently intake is ad-hoc (emails, notes in Deals or Zendesk) which leads to duplicated asks, inconsistent scoping, and missed prioritization signals. This ticket scopes a coordinated approach: a request collector template + triage rubric + lightweight scoping worksheet + visibility dashboard.

Goals:
- Provide Sales/CS a single place and a standard template to submit enterprise feature requests.
- Implement a 5-minute rapid-scope process that yields a one-page request summary and an initial priority score.
- Reduce time from first customer mention to Product triage from weeks to <= 72 hours for high-value requests.
- Surface data for Quarterly prioritization: estimated revenue impact, number of customers asking, alignment with strategic initiatives.

Non-Goals: We are not designing full PRD or implementation plans here. This is intake and initial scoping only.

Deliverables:
1) Request template (Form + email + Slack shortcut) with required fields and examples.
2) Triage rubric (scoring matrix: strategic fit, revenue/opportunity, technical complexity, compliance/regulatory risk, number of customers).
3) One-page scoping worksheet capturing acceptance criteria, success metrics, rough engineering signals, and blockers.
4) CS/Sales-facing guidance doc and 30-minute training deck.
5) A lightweight dashboard (Confluence/Sheets or Looker) that aggregates submissions and visualizes top requests by score and ARR potential.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria below.

Notes: We'll pilot with three AE/CS teams (Enterprise West, Strategic Accounts, PS-led deals) for 6 weeks. Champion: Liam (Product) + Maria (Sales Ops).
acceptance_criteria: Request template deployed and accessible to Sales/CS (Form + Slack shortcut)
Triage rubric documented with scoring examples and at least 6 internally validated samples
Pilot completed with >= 12 requests and feedback collected from AE/CS teams
Dashboard visualizing submissions, score distribution, and top 10 requests by estimated ARR
Handoff pattern validated: Product owner acknowledges high-score items within 72 hours with next-steps (research, discovery, or backlog slot)
One-pager scoping worksheet completed for at least 4 high-score requests during pilot
proposed_workflow: 1) Submission: AE/CS fills the request form (required fields: customer name, account ARR, urgency, user problem, desired outcome, success metrics, attachments). 2) Auto-enrich: Sales Ops populates account tier and ARR, and CS adds deal link. 3) Rapid-scope (Product): Product owner performs 5-minute intake using the scoping worksheet and assigns triage score. 4) Weekly Triage: Product and Eng rota review high-scoring items; decide: 'Research', 'Design spike', 'Backlog', or 'Not a priority'. 5) Handoff: For items moving to 'Research' or 'Backlog', create a ticket (PM- or ENG- key) and link original submission. 6) Feedback loop: Notify submitting AE/CS of outcome and expected timeline. 7) Quarterly rollup: aggregate scores to influence roadmap and Dedicated/Private offerings.
open_questions: Should ARR thresholds be handled as absolute numbers or % of account growth?
Do we need legal/contract involvement at intake for requests with SLA impacts?
Where should intake forms live long-term: Confluence form, Salesforce custom object, or internal portal?
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Duplicate requests across channels -> Mitigation: add unique request ID and link to deal record
Risk: Over-indexing on single large customer -> Mitigation: require product to flag strategic-only requests and create separate review cadence
Risk: Engineering capacity surprises -> Mitigation: include rough complexity banding in rapid-scope (Low/Med/High) and require Eng ack for High)
updates: 2025-02-16: Kickoff with Sales Ops and CS completed; Maria to prepare mapping of top 120 enterprise accounts.
2025-02-17: Draft intake form created; included fields for ARR, compliance flags, and existing workarounds.
2025-02-18: Triage rubric v0.1 circulated to Eng leads for feedback (requesting a simpler complexity axis).
2025-02-20: Pilot cohort identified (Enterprise West, Strategic, PS). Scheduled 30-minute enablement for 2025-02-25; target to start pilot 2025-02-26.
comments: Liam Chen: Focus the rubric on measurable signals (ARR, # customers, lift to retention). Avoid making it a popularity contest.
Maria Gonzalez: Sales need a Slack shortcut and a short checklist they can paste into deal notes.
Sabrina Lee: Engineering asks that any request flagged 'High' complexity must include a short list of affected systems and data privacy concerns.
next_steps: Finalize form and Slack shortcut (owner: Maria)
Lock triage rubric after Eng feedback (owner: Liam)
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on the triage rubric wording and required form fields. Sales/Ops input is critical to keep friction low. Engineering should confirm complexity band definitions.
